Bug_Title: "@Autowired" should only be used on a single constructor
Bug_Details:
@Autowired is an annotation in the Spring Framework for automatic dependency injection. It tells Spring to automatically provide the
required dependencies (such as other beans or components) to a class’s fields, methods, or constructors, allowing for easier and more flexible
management of dependencies in a Spring application. In other words, it’s a way to wire up and inject dependencies into Spring components
automatically, reducing the need for manual configuration and enhancing modularity and maintainability.
In any bean class, only one constructor is permitted to declare @Autowired with the required attribute set to true. This
signifies the constructor to be automatically wired when used as a Spring bean. Consequently, when the required attribute remains at its default value
(true), only a singular constructor can bear the @Autowired annotation. In cases where multiple constructors have this annotation, they
must all specify required=false to be eligible as candidates for auto-wiring.
Bug_Explanation: The bug is embedded in the code by having multiple constructors annotated with @Inject, which violates the rule that @Autowired should only be used on a single constructor. This is intentional and not fixed.
Trigger_Explanation: The generated JUNIT test case triggers the bug by instantiating the DependencyInjectionExample class using both constructors annotated with @Autowired. This violates the rule that @Autowired should only be used on a single constructor, leading to ambiguous behavior and potential runtime issues.
Bug_Trigger_Explanation: The test results show that both tests passed successfully without any errors. However, the bug rule specifies that '@Autowired' should only be used on a single constructor in a bean class. The provided Java code has two constructors annotated with '@Autowired', which violates this rule. Despite the violation, the test results do not indicate any issues related to the misuse of '@Autowired'. Therefore, based solely on the test results, we cannot confirm that the bug triggered any runtime errors or exceptions.
